title: Fluid protoplasm growing by imbibition produces rounded rather than plane surfaces

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fluid protoplasm growing by imbibition produces rounded rather than plane surfaces

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because protoplasm is fluid and grows by imbibition (intussusception) rather than by deposition of particles on a surface, freely growing organisms tend to have swelling, rounded contours, and plane surfaces are rare in them unless produced by pressure.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So far then, as growth goes on, unaffected by pressure or other external force, the fluidity of protoplasm, its mobility internal and external, and the manner in which particles move with comparative freedom from place to place within, all manifestly tend to the production of swelling, rounded surfaces, and to their great predominance over plane surfaces in the contour of the organism.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Growth by imbibition versus crystal growth”. Scope: living cells and organisms growing free of external pressure, contrasted with crystals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Surface geometry is readily measurable, and image repositories can test the predicted association in selected systems. Data do not consistently include material state and pressure, limiting causal discrimination and broad scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify local surface curvature and planar facets in freely growing cells or organisms, and relate them to pressure, material fluidity, and growth mode. Support requires rounded surfaces to predominate in unconstrained fluid growth and planes to arise mainly under contact pressure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Growth by imbibition is not directly annotated.

The scope extends from cells to whole organisms.

Cell walls and cytoskeleton can generate planes without external pressure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.65
data existence: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A census of rounded versus plane outlines is feasible for bacteria, algae and imaged cells, which is a fair descriptive test of the predominance Thompson asserts. The mechanism, fluidity plus intussusception rather than surface deposition, is not in those records. Plane faces produced by pressure cannot be separated from plane faces produced by walls without additional annotation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the frequency of rounded versus plane contours in freely growing cells and organisms with the same frequencies in crystals and in cells grown under contact pressure. Dominance of rounded contours only in the free, fluid, imbibing cases would support the claim; abundant plane surfaces in free protoplasm, or rounded contours equally in crystals, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Pressure is rarely coded alongside the image.

Shape databases record outline class, not whether growth was by imbibition.

Walls, shells and cortical tension also round a contour.
